related_questions.question: Are any COVID-19 vaccines FDA approved?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, some COVID-19 vaccines have received full FDA approval. Specifically, both the Pfizer-BioNTech (Comirnaty) and Moderna (Spikevax) vaccines have been fully approved by the FDA. Additionally, the FDA has approved updated versions of these vaccines for the 2024-2025 formula, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov).

list.title: Comirnaty (Pfizer-BioNTech):
list.snippet: The FDA approved the Comirnaty vaccine for individuals 12 years of age and older.

list.title: Spikevax (Moderna):
list.snippet: The FDA also approved Spikevax for individuals 12 years of age and older.

list.title: Updated mRNA vaccines:
list.snippet: The FDA has approved and authorized updated mRNA COVID-19 vaccines for the 2024-2025 formula, which are intended to better protect against currently circulating variants. These updated vaccines include both Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna's formulations.

list.title: EUA:
list.snippet: While the primary focus is on full approval, the FDA has also issued Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for some COVID-19 vaccines, allowing for their use in specific populations while full approval is pending. For example, there is an EUA amendment for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine (2024-2025 Formula) according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (.gov).

list.title: Safety monitoring:
list.snippet: The FDA continues to monitor the safety and effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and has required updated labeling for mRNA vaccines to include information about myocarditis and pericarditis.

related_questions.question: What is the FDA statement on the COVID vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: The FDA has updated the prescribing information for Comirnaty (Pfizer) and Spikevax (Moderna) mRNA COVID-19 vaccines to include new safety information about myocarditis and pericarditis risks. These updates, required by the FDA, incorporate the estimated incidence of these conditions following the 2023-2024 vaccine formula and the results of a study on cardiac MRI in affected individuals according to the FDA. The information is also included in the Adverse Reactions section and in materials for recipients and caregivers. The risk of myocarditis is reportedly higher in young men, according to a YouTube video from July 1, 2025.

text_blocks.snippet: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved and authorized for emergency use updated COVID-19 vaccines for the 2024-2025 formula. These updated vaccines are designed to provide better protection against circulating COVID-19 variants. Specifically, the following vaccines have been authorized: Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine (2024-2025 Formula) for individuals 6 months through 11 years of age, Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted (2024-2025 Formula) for individuals 12 years of age and older, and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine (2024-2025 Formula) for individuals 6 months through 11 years of age.

Additionally, the FDA has approved updated labeling for mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, including Comirnaty (Pfizer-BioNTech) and Spikevax (Moderna), to include new safety information about the risks of myocarditis and pericarditis following vaccination.
